People we stand on

2026-07-25 · written by alvin

None of this is original. We are standing on a long line of people who thought a computer should be a tool you could fully own.

  • IBM and the mainframe shops. They built multi-user machines when “sharing a computer” was the only way most humans would ever touch one. Time-sharing, terminals, remote login: the idea that a box could be a place, not only a desk ornament.

  • Bell Labs and Unix. Small tools, composable interfaces, the assumption that users are adults.

  • The free software and open source people. Source you can read. Systems you can rebuild. A culture that still believes understanding is part of using.

  • Public access Unix, tilde clubs, shell accounts, university clusters. Generations of nerds who gave strangers a home directory and a prompt because that was how you learned.

  • Forum elders and mailing-list ghosts. The ones who answered the same question for the tenth time without turning it into content.

Tharavad is a small thank-you to that lineage, and a small door for whoever is 13 (or 31) and still wishes they had a box. We cannot reverse the feed. We can still keep a house open. TinkerHub put the roof on; the rest of us get to bang on the walls.
